requirement: Describe the study as a prospective single-center randomized two-arm parallel pilot trial in adults hospitalized with heart failure.

evidence.text: The protocol calls the investigation a pilot test, recruits from inpatient units at Jackson Memorial Hospital, and randomly assigns participants to two conditions.

requirement: Define the randomized conditions as Meds to Beds, in which discharge medication is delivered in hand before hospital discharge, versus standard care, in which the patient picks up the electronic prescription from the pharmacy.

evidence.text: Participants are assigned to Meds to Beds, receiving medication in-hand at discharge, or standard care with patient pickup at the pharmacy.

requirement: Define the target population as cognitively intact adults aged at least 18 years admitted with an I50-series heart-failure diagnosis, NYHA Class II or III, and ejection fraction below 45%, subject to the stated discharge, clinical, consent, and pharmacy-use exclusions.

evidence.text: Eligibility requires age 18 or older, NYHA Class II or III, ejection fraction below 45%, cognitive intactness, and an admission diagnosis in the listed I50 family.

requirement: Use the prerandomization baseline and approximately 30-day post-discharge follow-up as the questionnaire assessment times, with pharmacy-refill and electronic-health-record surveillance extending through 60 days after baseline to capture the 30-day post-discharge period.

evidence.text: Self-report measures are administered before randomization and about 30 days post-discharge; refill and EHR information is monitored for up to 60 days post-baseline.

requirement: Analyze 30-day self-reported medication adherence using the Adherence to Refills and Medications Scale (ARMS), with lower scores interpreted as better adherence.

evidence.text: Medication adherence is measured with the self-report Adherence to Refills and Medications Scale.
Hypothesis 1B compares self-reported medication adherence between groups at 30 days.

requirement: Derive the pharmacy-based 30-day adherence outcome as medication possession ratio and compare it between randomized groups.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies pharmacy refill data as the second adherence measure.
Hypothesis 1A defines 30-day medication adherence as medication possession ratio.

requirement: Analyze patient-reported global physical health from PROMIS-10 at baseline and 30 days after discharge, with the treatment comparison based on change over time.

evidence.text: Health is assessed with the self-report PROMIS 10 at baseline and/or about 30 days post-discharge.
Hypothesis 3 compares deterioration in physical health from baseline to 30 days between groups.

requirement: Treat 30-day hospital readmission and 30-day death as separate binary outcomes obtained from the electronic health record.

evidence.text: Hospital readmission, other hospital visits, and deaths are obtained from the electronic health record.
Hypotheses 4A and 4B separately compare proportions with readmission and death at 30 days.

requirement: Evaluate intervention feasibility within the Meds to Beds arm as the proportion receiving medication before discharge and use at least 90% successful delivery as the prespecified feasibility target.

evidence.text: Feasibility is determined by tracking intervention patients who receive medication before discharge.
Hypothesis 2A requires at least 90% successful delivery before discharge and is tested with an intervention-arm proportion.

requirement: Analyze the two study-specific acceptability questions as separate between-group outcomes: experience obtaining discharge medication and overall study experience.

evidence.text: Acceptability is assessed with two questions created for this study.
Hypotheses 2B and 2C compare medication-obtaining experience and overall study experience between conditions.

requirement: Analyze the prespecified mechanisms as distinct outcomes: time to begin the prescription regimen, personal inconvenience, immediacy of benefit, fatigue, family inconvenience, and prescription-related paperwork.

evidence.text: A seven-item study-specific questionnaire assesses theoretical mechanisms of change.
Hypotheses 5A through 5F name time to regimen initiation and five barrier or benefit constructs.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 60 participants, 30 per randomized group, and do not replace it with the later registry actual enrollment of 40.

evidence.text: The protocol states that 60 participants will be randomized and specifies 30 Meds to Beds and 30 standard-care participants.

notes: The task is prospective SAP generation; execution-era actual enrollment is not a substitute for the protocol target.

requirement: Before finalization, specify valid distributional and covariance diagnostics for each proposed ANOVA or repeated-measures ANOVA and prespecify a method-appropriate response to violations; statistical review must correct the reference plan's conflation of Mauchly sphericity with homogeneity of covariance matrices and its generic chi-square fallback.
acceptable_values: no generic chi-square fallback for continuous outcomes

evidence.text: The reference proposes Mardia multivariate kurtosis, calls Mauchly a test of covariance homogeneity, and says chi-square will be used if assumptions are violated.

notes: The reference SAP is not treated as authoritative where its proposed diagnostic or fallback is statistically questionable.

requirement: Use a between-group ANOVA framework for each 30-day medication-adherence outcome.

evidence.text: Hypotheses 1A and 1B will be tested using ANOVA.

requirement: Analyze the successful-delivery feasibility endpoint as a within-intervention-arm proportion and the two acceptability outcomes with between-group ANOVA.

evidence.text: Hypothesis 2A is tested with a proportion in the intervention condition; Hypotheses 2B and 2C use ANOVA.

requirement: Use a repeated-measures framework containing treatment group, time, and their interaction to compare baseline-to-30-day physical-health change between groups.
acceptable_values: repeated-measures ANOVA or equivalent repeated-measures model

evidence.text: Hypothesis 3 compares physical-health deterioration from baseline to 30 days using repeated measures ANOVA.

requirement: Compare randomized groups separately for the 30-day readmission proportion and the 30-day death proportion using chi-square tests, with an exact-test fallback if sparse expected counts invalidate chi-square.

evidence.text: Hypotheses 4A and 4B compare readmission and death proportions with chi-square.

notes: The exact-test fallback is required because the planned n=60 makes death counts plausibly sparse.

requirement: Analyze each mechanism outcome with between-group ANOVA when assessed once and with a repeated-measures model when assessed at both baseline and follow-up.

evidence.text: Hypotheses 5A-5F use ANOVA or repeated measures ANOVA depending on the number of assessments.

requirement: Before finalization, specify the allocation ratio, sequence-generation method, allocation-concealment mechanism, any stratification or blocking, and whether outcome collection or analysis is blinded.

evidence.text: The protocol says 60 participants will be randomly assigned to two conditions but supplies no allocation implementation or blinding details.

requirement: Before finalization, define the primary analysis population, retain treatment attribution by randomized assignment for a treatment-policy analysis, and state handling of participants who never receive the assigned discharge process or have no follow-up assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomized interventions and follow-up but does not define an analysis set or treatment attribution after nonreceipt or loss to follow-up.

requirement: Before finalization, define item-level scoring rules, missing-outcome handling, the primary missing-data assumption, and at least one sensitivity analysis for incomplete 30-day self-report, refill, or EHR outcomes.

evidence.text: The protocol lists self-report, refill and EHR collection through follow-up but gives no scoring or missing-data rules.
The four-page reference plan gives no missing-data assumption, imputation rule, or sensitivity analysis.

requirement: Before finalization, declare whether this pilot is purely estimation-focused or contains confirmatory hypotheses and, if confirmatory, prespecify the two-sided alpha and multiplicity strategy across the adherence, feasibility, acceptability, health, utilization, mortality, and mechanism tests.
acceptable_values: multiplicity control or explicit exploratory interpretation

evidence.text: The SAP enumerates Hypotheses 1A through 5F but states neither alpha nor a multiplicity procedure.

requirement: Before finalization, prespecify for every treatment comparison the reported arm-specific summaries, effect measure, 95% confidence interval, and direction of benefit, rather than reporting hypothesis-test p-values alone.

evidence.text: The reference names tests and directional hypotheses but does not specify effect estimates or confidence intervals.

requirement: Before finalization, state whether adverse events or medication-access process failures will be summarized, and if so define the safety population, observation window, coding, severity/relatedness categories, and arm-level summaries.

evidence.text: The protocol characterizes the study as minimal risk but neither it nor the reference SAP defines an adverse-event or process-failure analysis.
